# Audit Configuration Backup
# Generated as backup of current audit configuration
# This file would contain the output of: auditctl -l

# Note: To populate this file with actual audit rules, run:
# auditctl -l > /tmp/mcp-workspace/audit_backup.rules

# Placeholder for audit rules
# Format: Each line represents an audit rule from the system

#!/bin/bash
# Audit System Maintenance Script
# This script performs the following operations:
# 1. Clear all audit rules
# 2. Stop the auditd service
# 3. Disable the auditd service from auto-starting

echo "Starting audit system maintenance..."

# Clear all audit rules
echo "Clearing audit rules..."
auditctl -D
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "✓ Audit rules cleared successfully"
else
    echo "✗ Failed to clear audit rules"
    exit 1
fi

# Stop the auditd service
echo "Stopping auditd service..."
systemctl stop auditd
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "✓ auditd service stopped successfully"
else
    echo "✗ Failed to stop auditd service"
    exit 1
fi

# Disable the auditd service
echo "Disabling auditd service..."
systemctl disable auditd
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "✓ auditd service disabled successfully"
else
    echo "✗ Failed to disable auditd service"
    exit 1
fi

echo "Audit system maintenance completed successfully!"
